title: Coefficient program output and cost
statement: Let $n,a,d,s$ be positive integers with $2a\le d$ and $s\ge1$, and consider a Boolean target on the sign cube of dimension $n$, together with a finite family $\mathcal F$ of subsets of the coordinates. The coefficient program returns the sparse Fourier hypothesis supported on $\mathcal F$ whose coefficient at each $U\in\mathcal F$ is the empirical average, over the program's small-bias sample, of the target value times the sign character indexed by $U$. Its cost has zero random examples, a number of membership queries equal to the sample count, and local work equal to the sample count plus the generator construction work and $|\mathcal F|$ times the local coefficient-estimation work.
hypotheses_covered: A Boolean target on the sign cube
A finite family of coordinate subsets
